documentation.rationale: Partial. There is a photographed (but undated, shop-unnamed) lift invoice and a claim of complete Sewell Lexus dealer history. However, there is no VIN, no attached Carfax and no service printout, so the identity half and the maintenance half are both largely unproven.

condition.rationale: Photos show clean paint, straight panels and a tidy interior with light driver-seat soiling. Nothing mechanical is proven: no SAI, KDSS, leak, fluid-service or underside evidence at 173k miles. 'Runs absolutely perfect' is not evidence.

price_value.rationale: $21,000 sits at the top of the $13,710–$21,554 fair-value range (mid $16,301). A comparable 2017 Premium at 165,800 mi sold for $17,750. Some of the premium is for the lift and coating, which add little value.

mission_fit.rationale: A body-on-frame V8 4WD with low range, a third row and roof rails fits the camping/RTT capability the RX lacks. The mild Eibach level suits light trail and rack use. Fit is held back by high mileage and unproven SAI/KDSS status.

logistics.rationale: Fort Worth, TX is a fly-and-drive trip of roughly 1,600 miles. PPI access is not stated, though DFW has the selling Lexus dealer and plenty of independents. CA registration is expected to be feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Attractive dark blue over tan with a sunroof, Premium trim and a quality-brand mild lift. The grille swap and remote start are cosmetic or convenience items. Otherwise a typical example.

positives: Seller states single-dealer (Sewell Lexus) service history since new, verifiable via Lexus records. Potentially strong documentation if the VIN is provided.
Photographed invoice shows the lift is a reputable Eibach Pro-Truck kit, with the correct supporting sway-bar drops, track-bar bracket and an alignment, not a cheap spacer lift.
Texas car with clean-looking paint and panels in photos; low inherent rust exposure.
Interior photos show light wear only. Second-row bench, third-row belts present, OEM cargo and floor mats.
Toyota/Lexus 1UR-FE platform suits high mileage better than most.

Unverified: transmission, transfer-case, differential and coolant service history (ask for the dealer service printout).

ppi_focus: Full scan including history and pending codes; cold-start check of the secondary air injection pump and valves (P2440–P2446)
KDSS cylinders, accumulator, lines and valve-body leakage; KDSS pressure and levelling after the lift
Lift install quality: CV boot angles and condition, upper ball joints and control arms, sway-bar drop and track-bar bracket hardware torque, alignment printout
Rear suspension configuration (air vs coil) and height-control function or warnings
Coolant seepage at the valley plate, timing cover and water pump; cooling system pressure test
Transmission, transfer-case and differential fluid condition; center diff lock and low-range engagement
Frame, crossmembers and hitch mounting for towing or impact damage; underbody condition
Brake rotors and pads, front lower control arm bushings and shocks at 173k miles
Tire date codes and wear pattern (alignment after lift)
Roof rail mounts and integrity for future rooftop tent use
what_would_change_verdict: VIN plus a dealer service printout showing on-time fluid services and any SAI or KDSS work would materially raise documentation.
A clean PPI with no SAI history codes, a dry KDSS and valley plate, and a sound lift install would raise condition.
A price closer to the $16–18k comps would improve value.
Down: SAI codes or pump noise, KDSS leaks, a botched lift install, towing wear, or Carfax accident entries.
evidence.mission_note: A GX460 squarely fits the utility/capability branch: body-on-frame 4WD with low range, a third row and roof rails supply the camping and rooftop-tent capability the RX lacks, and the mild Eibach level is a modest positive at most. At 173k miles its value rests on proving the dealer history and the SAI/KDSS status.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a dark blue 2017 GX460 with a tan interior in Fort Worth, TX at $21,000 with 173,333 claimed miles. Photos show clean paint, a light-wear interior, a 2020+-style grille swap, side steps and a rear hitch. A photographed but undated invoice with no shop name confirms an Eibach Pro-Truck lift with sway-bar drop mounts, a rear track-bar bracket and an alignment. The seller claims complete Sewell Lexus dealer service history and a clean Carfax title, but provides neither the VIN nor any record, so both remain claims. The model-critical items are open: SAI history, KDSS condition after the lift, coolant seepage and underside condition are undocumented, and 'zero check engine lights' is seller prose. The asking price sits at the top of the mileage-adjusted fair-value range, above a comparable 2017 Premium sale at $17,750. Nothing observed indicates a specific fault; the open questions are documentation and inspection items.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, the Sewell Lexus service printout and the full dated lift invoice, and ask whether a PPI at a DFW shop of your choosing is allowed before any deposit.
